column1: # Hebrew (he) catalog. Columns, separated by a TAB:  context <TAB> source <TAB> translation
#   context  empty                a plain UI string; `source` is the English text in the code
#            @id                  a command id (e.g. file.saveAs): wins over the English text for
#                                 that menu item, so one id can read differently from its twin
#            @plural              `source` is "one|other" (English forms); the translation lists the
#                                 language's forms separated by "|" (see `plural` in i18n/mod.rs):
#            anything else        a disambiguating context passed to `tr_ctx`
#   escapes  \n  \t  \\  inside a column. `{name}` placeholders must appear in both columns.
#   lines starting with # and blank lines are ignored.
# Clean-room: every entry was written from the plain meaning of the English label using ordinary
# Israeli Hebrew computing vocabulary. No proprietary localisation resource, string table or
# product UI (Acrobat's included) was consulted or copied; add entries the same way.
# Gender-neutral: commands and buttons are verbal nouns (שמירה, פתיחה…), instructions are
# impersonal (יש לבחור…, ניתן ל…), never a gendered imperative.
# Product and technology names (PdfCraft, PDF, Acrobat JavaScript ...) stay in Latin letters;
# the trailing "…" of dialog commands is kept. Digits are Western (0-9). Keyboard key caps (Ctrl,
# Shift, Esc ...) stay as printed on Hebrew keyboards.
# Write every entry in logical (typing) order, without direction marks. The text layout reads each entry right to left
# (the vendored epaint's bidi patch); i18n/mod.rs starts it with a right-to-left mark
# (bidi::rtl_label), so an entry that begins with a placeholder or a Latin name still does.
